#1822. What will happen if Man United get relegated from the Premier League?

By Ben Knapton | 09 Nov 2026 10:04

Setting unwanted record after unwanted record under the beleaguered Michael Carrick, Manchester United - one of the most revered clubs to ever grace the English game - are facing the very real threat of losing their perpetual Premier League status.

Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa may have seen the Red Devils exhibit their fabulous fightback powers once more, but it also left them celebrating just one win from their first 10 top-flight games of the season, ensuring that they would spend the November international break in the bottom three of the Premier League table.

Only one point separates 18th-placed Man United from rock-bottom Crystal Palace, 16th-placed Nottingham Forest and 17th-placed Coventry City, and the powers-that-be will reportedly hold a meeting to discuss Carrick's future during the domestic hiatus.

A change in management ultimately prevented Tottenham Hotspur from suffering an unthinkable relegation last season, but what if the worst should happen to Man United?

Here, Sports Mole takes a look at what is likely to happen if the Red Devils drop down to the Championship for the 2027-28 season.

It was only a matter of weeks ago that Man United announced record revenues of £677.6m for the 2026 fiscal year, albeit alongside a pre-tax loss of £43m, thanks to their third-placed Premier League finish in 2025-26 and a wave of cost-cutting measures.

However, Man Utd's Championship revenue is estimated to fall to around £375m to £450m, largely thanks to a sharp decline in broadcasting revenues from the loss of Premier League TV deals.

The Red Devils recently recorded £206.8m in broadcasting revenue, but that number is projected to fall to around £55m to £65m in the second tier, and there would also be no European broadcasting boost unless they shock the continent and win the 2026-27 Champions League to qualify for next year's edition.

Man United would also have to reduce ticket prices, potentially bringing their matchday revenue down from just over £150m to just over £100m, although playing 23 home matches rather than 19 - plus the potential of playoffs - would negate that specific impact marginally.

Commercial deals would also suffer a hit, due to expected performance clauses in contracts with kit suppliers and other club sponsors, so a plethora of player sales would be inevitable in order to navigate the massive economical hit as smoothly as possible.

Carrick retains the backing of a large portion of the Man United fanbase, the players are currently receiving mixed receptions, but INEOS and the Glazer family could hardly be held in less esteemed regard.

However, Man Utd fans wondering whether relegation could be the straw that breaks the owners' back are likely to be left disappointed, as the Glazers are not predicted to sell the club even if they drop down to the Championship.

As businessmen, United's owners are supposedly waiting for the perfect moment to cash in on Man Utd, when the club's value is at its highest; in an ideal world, this would be when the Red Devils have moved into their proposed new stadium and are competing in the Champions League, not when they are languishing in the second tier.

INEOS would not survive in its current state, though; sporting director Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada would almost certainly be moved on, but Ratcliffe could alternatively try to increase his stake in the club while it is at its cheapest; however, that could not happen until 2029.

Interest from the Middle East reportedly remains after Sheikh Jassim's failed takeover bid too, and attempts to wrestle control from Ratcliffe and the Glazers could ramp up as the club's value declines.

Few are expecting Carrick to still be in charge of Man United come 2027, and the current favourites to succeed the Englishman include Mauricio Pochettino, Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

Roberto De Zerbi affirmed that he would stay at Spurs even if they were relegated last season; the Italian's loyalties were not tested to that extreme, but others' very well could be.

Neither Conte nor Pochettino would be prepared to take on a second-tier project, and the same is almost certainly true of Nagelsmann, although the 39-year-old's youth makes him a slightly more realistic option for a season in the Championship.

Instead, Howe could welcome the opportunity to rebuild the Red Devils, having already guided Bournemouth up the divisions with a limited budget while also taking charge of Burnley for three Championship campaigns.

A viable alternative to Howe is ex-Red Devils assistant and youth manager Kieran McKenna - formerly linked with the United job in 2024 - as the 40-year-old is also unattached, knows the culture of the club and guided Ipswich Town to two Premier League promotions between 2021 and 2026.

Man United players would supposedly not have to worry about any wage cuts in the Championship, as their contracts do not contain specific relegation clauses allowing the Red Devils to slash their salaries.

However, with the next Euros, Copa America and Africa Cup of Nations on the horizon, a mass exodus of big names would be unavoidable, especially with the Red Devils also needing to significantly reduce their operating costs too.

Offloading young players, or those just approaching their prime, would do wonders for the club's financial picture, so Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko, Carlos Baleba and Senne Lammens could all be moved on.

Leny Yoro, Kobbie Mainoo and Patrick Dorgu would generate decent sale figures too, but it is not impossible to envisage the young trio sticking around for the rebuild project, if they are willing to accept the potential knock-on effects for Euro 2028 selection.

The club's two highest earners - Bruno Fernandes and Marcus Rashford - would also have to take major pay cuts or depart, and both could therefore be tempted by Saudi Pro League switches despite their deep connection to the Theatre of Dreams.

Fernandes is part of a large group out of contract in 2027 too - a list that also includes Harry Maguire, Tom Heaton, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw - and none should be in line for a renewal if relegation is on the cards.

Joshua Zirkzee, Matthijs de Ligt, Noussair Mazraoui, Manuel Ugarte, Diogo Dalot and Youri Tielemans should all be on the market too, but the same cannot be said for the up-and-coming Carrington prospects.

Expect Ayden Heaven, Shea Lacey, Harry Amass and Jack & Tyler Fletcher to stick around and play central roles in Man United's second-tier season, potentially alongside the returning Chido Obi and Dan Gore, as well as veteran shot-stopper Karl Darlow.

#1821. ‘It didn’t sit very well’ – Baena admits Alvarez transfer request irked Atleti team-mates

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Atletico Madrid midfielder Alex Baena admits Julian Alvarez's attempts to join Barcelona this summer "annoyed" the rest of Diego Simeone's squad.

Alvarez was at the heart of one of the most high-profile sagas during the summer transfer window, after saying it was his "dream" to join Barca.

Barca president Joan Laporta was not shy about the club's desire to acquire the former World Cup winner, but the Atleti hierarchy responded by saying they would never do a deal with their domestic rivals.

Ultimately, Alvarez stayed put, with Barca moving for Gabriel Jesus at the end of the window, to provide competition for Raphinha, Lamine Yamal, Fermin Lopez, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi.

The Argentine's return to the fold saw him booed by his own fans during a draw with Villarreal in August, but he has since been fully reintegrated by head coach Diego Simeone.

Yet Baena said the way Alvarez approached the speculation did not earn him much support in Atleti's dressing room.

"It feels a bit strange when a team-mate says publicly that he wants to leave," the Spain international said in an interview with Cadena SER.

"I can understand a player having doubts if a club like Barca or Real Madrid comes in for you, but, ultimately, it was the way he went about it that really annoyed us at Atletico."

Reporting for duty with @SEFutbol  https://t.co/WUkeGwGcHr

— Atlético de Madrid (@atletienglish) November 10, 2026

Now, though, Baena says all has been forgiven and Alvarez deserves to be supported by everyone at the club.

"We would have supported him regardless of what he decided to do," Baena added.

"The important thing is that he is with us now, and we need to show him all the affection in the world."

Alvarez has netted just twice in all competitions this season while providing three assists, having teed up Giuliano Simeone's opening goal in Sunday's 2-1 defeat to Barca.

Alvarez led all Atletico players for shots (four), touches in the opposition box (seven) and successful dribbles (three) in that game, while also creating two chances.

Atletico's defeat snapped their seven-game winning run in LaLiga. They sit third in the table, two points behind second-place Real Madrid and five adrift of leaders Barca.

Alvarez could feature for Argentina during the international break, as they face Uruguay and Costa Rica in friendlies, while Baena and his Spain team-mates will take on Czechia and England in the Nations League.

#1820. Portugal boss Jorge Jesus claims Cristiano Ronaldo did NOT tell him he was retiring from international duty after fallout with superstar: 'I found out the same time as you'

Published: 16:01 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 16:09 EST, 6 November 2026

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insists he does not 'feel guilty' about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement and had no idea it was coming.

Ronaldo's explosive row with Jesus that escalated after he was left on the bench for a Nations League game and climaxed with the 41-year-old publishing a long statement hammering his manager, left their relationship in tatters.

And on Thursday, weeks after the dispute, Ronaldo announced his retirement from Portugal duty, bringing a sad end to his career on the international stage.

Jesus has now spoken for the first time about it, saying at a press conference: 'I don't feel guilty about anything regarding his departure. I respect his decision and, as such, his history cannot be ignored.

'I will never do that. Because he will always be a symbol, and I have built a strong friendship with him over this year and a half. Sporting-wise, he has now made another decision, and I greatly respect his decision.'

When asked if he thought he was the reason for Ronaldo's retirement, the 72-year-old added: 'No... Maybe I rushed things, but not because of me. It was in his head that, with more or less call-ups, this was going to happen. It was always going to be during my tenure.

Jorge Jesus, pictured at a press conference on Friday, said he did not feel guilty about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement

'I didn't speak to Ronaldo because I was thinking about calling him up. From that moment on, I was going to have time to talk to him.'

And Jesus insisted he had no idea why Ronaldo chose now to quit, adding: 'You have to ask him... The absolute certainty I have is that Cris worked with me for a year. We were happy at the club where we were, we were champions. I respect his decision at this moment.

'He would always have been with me throughout all these years that we were going to work together. He was the one who would decide. I don't know why he made that decision. What I do know is that he knew his time was coming, he was the one who would choose. And he chose. Only he can answer that better than I can.'

Ronaldo scored a world record 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal and won the 2016 European Championship as well as two Nations League titles.

But he will not add to those achievements now – instead stepping away after 23 years playing for his country.

In his retirement statement, he admitted that he had at times 'failed' and revealed that his decision was difficult, but felt proud of his work and willing to hand over the number seven jersey.

His final minutes in a Portugal shirt came against Wales in September, when he played 67 minutes in a 1-0 Nations League win over Wales.

After being left on the bench for their subsequent match against Norway, Ronaldo had a row with manager Jesus and flew away from Portugal's camp via his private jet.

Ronaldo never reached a World Cup final and cried after Portugal were knocked out by Spain in the last 16 over the summer

Marking his retirement, he wrote: 'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.'

There will be questions over the way Ronaldo's international career has ended – to the public, it appears to be on rather bitter terms.

Ronaldo was livid after being left on the bench despite warming-up for Portugal's Nations League win over Norway on September 27 – the first time he has been an unused substitute during his 23-year international career.

The highlight of his Portugal career was lifting the 2016 European Championship, even if he got injured in the final

That led to him skipping three training sessions and abandoning the camp for Portugal's last two matches of the international break, fleeing to Spain via private jet.

He did not even watch their next match against Norway because he was soaring away on his plane with his family.

The former Manchester United star was vexed at how Jesus had handled his press conference after leaving him on the bench.

Ronaldo insisted that Jesus had broken a promise to apologise to the 'Portuguese people' and his team-mates for not bringing him on.

He claimed he had been guaranteed 30 minutes of football against Norway after the Portuguese FA persuaded him not to retire following the World Cup.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner even offered to retire if that was what the coach and head of Portuguese FA wanted, only for them to reiterate their desire to have him.

But most hurtfully, Ronaldo released a stinging 1,996-word statement accusing Jesus of 'broken promises'. He said the manager had agreed to deliver an eight-point mea culpa taking responsibility for leaving him on the bench after a supposed pact to play him.

Jesus did concede it was a mistake to make him warm up but gave a different narrative of events, saying: 'The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.'

In the end, Ronaldo was fined £215 by the Portuguese FA and technically banned for a month – though that was backdated, making him free for their upcoming fixtures. But fans – and the man himself – will now have to embrace the next chapter as Portugal aim to move on without the most illustrious player in their history.

#1819. Opposition insight for Genoa-Milan: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

Genoa are the next opponents for AC Milan and given the Rossoblu’s recent form, they certainly could have faced them at a better time.

Ruben Amorim and his men really need to pick themselves up with a win tomorrow afternoon, which would at least allow them to build on the derby win in the league. In the Europa League, however, that chance is already gone as they lost to Ferencvaros.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, getting the three points might not be the easiest task as Genoa have been in red-hot form lately, and will certainly use all of the support from their fans at the Marassi tomorrow.

➤ Manager: Daniele De Rossi ➤ Form (all comps): W-L-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Osmajic – 4 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Colombo and El Shaarawy – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: None.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was bought permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but did make sure to express his respect for the Rossoneri.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

#1818. Chelsea transfer news: Blues outcast 'targeted' by Roma after Gian Piero Gasperini request

By Darren Plant | 09 Nov 2026 10:26

Chelsea winger Jamie Gittens has reportedly remained as a serious transfer target for Roma.

During the summer window, the former Borussia Dortmund attacker emerged as a potential signing for the Italian giants, who had secured a return to the Champions League.

However, not only did a suitable proposal not arrive, the England Under-21 international was given a chance by new Blues boss Xabi Alonso during pre-season.

While the 22-year-old would have hoped for regular opportunities under the Spaniard, he had made just one start and one substitute outing in the EFL Cup before suffering an ankle injury during the last international break.

With Gittens remaining on the sidelines ever since, it is yet to be determined whether he will make an impact upon his return.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Roma are preparing to make a fresh approach for Gittens at the turn of the year.

Last week, head coach Gian Piero Gasperini claimed that he needed more Champions League-ready players to be added to his squad.

That was in response to Roma giving up a two-goal lead against Manchester United, the second time that his team had let slip a commanding advantage having also done the same versus Real Madrid.

Despite scoring goals having not been Roma's problem this season, they are still keen to add Gittens to the first-team ranks at Stadio Olimpico.

Like in the summer, Roma would prefer to negotiate a loan deal for Gittens, rather than pay a substantial fee for his signature.

Since picking up a serious hamstring injury at the end of January, Gittens has not made a single appearance in the Premier League.

Even when he returns to fitness, there is little prospect of him earning regular starts under Alonso, particularly when Chelsea are only playing Premier League games until January.

The aim now should be trying to protect his £50m+ transfer fee by allowing him to go elsewhere and play games, wherever that may be.

With teams prepared to pay a loan fee for his signature, it should be an easy exit to facilitate.

#1816. Rangers hitman Ryan Naderi is finding his groove at the ideal time... and he could hold the key in Ibrox trophy hunt

Published: 15:06 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 16:27 EST, 6 November 2026

Back in February, Danny Rohl’s decision to tell the Rangers supporters that his latest signing Ryan Naderi reminded him of a certain Thomas Muller was met with widespread derision.

Quite right too. In truth, those comments still sound every bit as silly as they did nine months ago.

However, while that will surely be the first and last time Naderi is likened to the German World Cup winner, Rohl at least appears to have been proven right in his assertion that the frontman had the tools to ultimately be a success at Ibrox.

Clearly, he saw something the rest of us couldn’t.

You would have got long odds on the newly-capped Czech international still being at the club by the time the summer transfer window shut in early September, such was the general feeling towards the big man after a thoroughly underwhelming start to life in Glasgow.

That Rangers were so keen to pay Hansa Rostock the best part of £5million to bring him over from the German third tier appeared somewhat foolish given that Naderi would go on to find the net just three times across all competitions, with two of those coming in an 8-0 rout of Queen’s Park in the Scottish Cup.

Naderi's winning goal against Aberdeen last weekend took his tally for the season to eight

Simply put, he played more like a headless chicken than a reliable Rangers striker.

The summer departure of the man who convinced the club to push the boat out to get him, followed by the arrival of Derek McInnes — not to mention new club skipper Lawrence Shankland — suggested his days may have already been numbered.

You’d have done well to find any Rangers fan who would have objected either.

But, in a very short time, Naderi has put the hard yards in to establish himself as an integral part of this Rangers team. In fact, he’s almost undroppable these days.

His late goal against Aberdeen last weekend to book Rangers’ place in the Premier Sports Cup final against Hibs next month was his eighth in 16 appearances this season.

Let’s not pretend that those numbers would be quite as impressive had the likes of Shankland and Youssef Chermiti been on the pitch rather than on the treatment table. Naderi probably knows that himself.

But all he can do in their absence is take advantage of the opportunity offered to him, and it’s so far so good in that sense.

It’s evident that he is a man playing with confidence, and his displays are night-and-day from what we saw last season.

McInnes has to take a fair share of the credit for the role he has played in Naderi turning his Ibrox career around. The manager’s style suits him to a tee.

Of course, there are all sorts of nuances and intricate details that go into his tactical ideology, but the general idea is pretty simple: Get the ball forward as quickly as possible.

Manager Derek McInnes has managed to get the best out of his Czech striker in recent months

There is very little faffing around in midfield under McInnes’ Rangers. None of this tippy-tappy nonsense. It was the same when he was in charge at Kilmarnock, and certainly a huge reason behind Hearts’ success last season too.

And Naderi — alongside Kevin Kelsy — is benefiting from a more direct approach which aims to turn the opposition around at every opportunity. It’s proven fairly effective until this point.

You would suspect the chances will keep coming with players such as Kim Min-su and Badredine Bouanani providing the ammunition, with the latter in particular really coming on to a game in recent weeks after taking some time to find his feet since making the loan switch from VfB Stuttgart.

Part of Naderi’s problem last season was that he was spending too much time outside the box in an effort to get involved in the build-up. Too eager to impress, perhaps.

In this team, he doesn’t need to do that anywhere near as often.

There’s no reason why he can’t hit double figures this year. In fact, it would now be considered a major disappointment if he failed to do so.

He’ll have a chance to boost his numbers on Saturday evening when he lines up against St Mirren. And he will no doubt fancy doing exactly that, having registered a goal and two assists against Craig McLeish’s men earlier this season.

With Celtic failing to extend their lead at the top of the table last weekend after falling to defeat in Falkirk, Rangers can move to within a point ahead of the defending champions’ meeting with Kilmarnock on Sunday.

They will need to be a damn sight better than they have been on their travels of late to do so, however. Back-to-back 2-2 draws on the road at Dundee and Hearts could prove costly further down the line in what’s shaping up to be a tight title race. They could have easily lost both.

They simply can’t afford to drop any more points, especially with Celtic continuing to look so vulnerable.

Rangers can't afford to drop more points after back-to-back away draws at Dundee and Hearts

You would assume Martin O’Neill’s men will find their groove eventually, so it is imperative that Rangers stay within striking distance until they face off again in the new year.

It should be an intriguing tussle in Paisley. The Buddies have earned plaudits for the way in which they have attempted to move away from the style employed under former boss Stephen Robinson.

And they have demonstrated on multiple occasions this season that they can be hard to stop when in full flow. They certainly gave Celtic a scare back in September before succumbing to a narrow 2-1 loss.

But they have undoubtedly taken a step back of late, winning just once in their last eight league fixtures.

Keeping Naderi quiet will be key to stopping the rot. There’s a statement you couldn’t possibly have envisaged reading not too long ago.

#1815. The 10 best footballers in the world: Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe ranked

By Andrew Delaney | 09 Nov 2026 10:29, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 10:29

A new king of the global game was crowned at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, with Bayern Munich's Harry Kane becoming the latest name to follow in the footsteps of football icons including Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo to claim the most prestigious individual prize of all.

Kane, 33, continues to find the back of the net at an impressive rate, netting 10 times in 15 appearances for Bayern this season, in addition to coming up with 10 assists.

Kane pipped the likes of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to become the latest first-time winner of the Ballon d'Or, but does that make the England international the current best player in the world in our eyes?

Here, Sports Mole casts its vote for the 10 greatest active footballers on the planet right now.

Few players illustrate just how much the game has changed over the past decade or so than Hakimi, whose attacking ability from right-back was a leading factor in Paris Saint-Germain finally ending their Champions League hoodoo in 2025 and then winning it again one year later.

Hakimi is the best full-back in world football and therefore had to make this list, as his form has been so important to back-to-back Champions League winners PSG.

Dembele is currently on the sidelines with a hamstring injury, but it would have been incredibly harsh to leave him out of this list given his standing in the game.

The France international has scored four goals and registered six assists in 10 appearances for PSG this term, and he will be vital to their chances of glory once again in 2026-27.

Haaland's overall performance level has been criticised in the early months of the 2026-27 campaign, but he has still come up with 14 goals in 14 appearances.

The Norway international is now on 176 goals and 30 assists in 212 appearances for Man City, with the 26-year-old simply a goal machine.

However, Man City's off-the-field issues could lead to his departure sooner rather than later.

Arsenal simply must have one representative in the top-10 list considering their form this season, and their indomitable midfield metronome gets the nod.

Perhaps the best compliment one can pay Declan Rice is that no-one is talking about his transfer fee as a waste of money, as the England international has been worth every penny of the £105m that Arsenal spent on him.

Devastating from any dead-ball situation, an unrelenting ball carrier and reliable in front of goal when the opportunity presents itself, Rice has helped elevate Arsenal to new levels.

Vitinha has played a vital role in Paris Saint-Germain winning back-to-back Champions League titles, and he is arguably the biggest midfield talent in world football.

Few can dictate a match in the way that the 26-year-old can, and his performances during the 2026-27 campaign have once again been of an incredibly high level.

Raphinha has been in incredible form for Barcelona this season, scoring 19 goals and registering three assists in 14 appearances in all competitions.

The Brazil international has thrived operating as a central attacker during the 2026-27 campaign, and there is no question that he is deserving of a spot in the top five of this particular list.

What an incredible talent Jude Bellingham is.

There were question marks surrounding just how good he is ahead of the 2026 World Cup, but he had an outstanding tournament for England.

The 23-year-old has scored five goals and registered four assists in 16 appearances for Real Madrid this season.

Kylian Mbappe has an incredible record of 103 goals and 15 assists in 119 appearances for Real Madrid following his move to Bernabeu from Paris Saint-Germain.

The 27-year-old has also netted 67 goals in 107 caps for France.

Mbappe's trophy cabinet since arriving at Real Madrid is the biggest disappointment and keeps him from being first or second here, but the attacker is an exceptional talent.

Where would Bayern Munich be without Harry Kane?

The England captain has been a revelation at Bayern since joining from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023, scoring a total of 156 goals and providing 43 assists in 162 appearances across all tournaments, with 102 of those strikes netted in just 103 Bundesliga matches.

Kane won the Bundesliga Golden Boot in his first two seasons with the German giants, and he recently secured the Ballon d'Or crown.

While not the recipient of the Ballon d’Or, there is only one player who can currently top this list, and it is Barcelona’s number 10: teenage superstar Lamine Yamal.

Making his Barca debut at 15, and becoming a regular at 16, Yamal is now 19, and his overall record for the Catalan giants stands at 62 goals and 64 assists in 176 appearances.

Yamal has won the European Championship and World Cup for Spain, and there is little doubting that he is currently the best player in world football.

#1814. Prediction: Italy vs France

Two of European football’s most decorated nations meet at San Siro on Thursday night as Italy host France in a crucial UEFA Nations League clash.

France lead Group A1 with 10 points from four matches, while Italy sit second on seven points. A French victory would guarantee top spot and secure qualification for the knockout stage, while the Azzurri need a positive result to strengthen their own position ahead of a decisive final-day trip to Belgium.

Roberto Mancini’s second spell in charge has produced encouraging signs after an initially difficult start.

Following a disappointing defeat to Belgium, the Azzurri responded impressively with victories over Turkey and a valuable draw away to France. Italy then followed that result with another win against Turkey, moving onto seven points and keeping qualification firmly in their own hands.

Captain Gianluigi Donnarumma was the standout performer in the reverse fixture against France, producing a series of excellent saves to secure a point in Paris. His experience could prove vital again against one of Europe’s most talented attacking units.

There is also growing excitement around Italy’s next generation. Pio Esposito continues to impress at senior level, while newcomers such as Mattia Liberali and Alphadjo Cisse have earned call-ups after strong starts to the season.

However, injuries remain a concern. Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Giacomo Raspadori, Moise Kean and Gianluca Mancini are all unavailable, forcing Mancini to continue reshaping his squad.

France have adapted quickly under Zinedine Zidane, after Didier Deschamps’ reign ended somewhan unceremoniously with the World Cup.

Apart from the draw against Italy, Les Bleus have been flawless in this Nations League campaign, recording victories over Belgium and Turkey to establish a three-point advantage at the top of the group.

Their latest success was especially impressive. Trailing Belgium late in the contest, France produced a devastating spell of attacking football, scoring four times in 15 minutes to transform the match completely.

The visitors possess immense quality throughout the squad, led by captain Kylian Mbappe, who remains the focal point of France’s attack. Marcus Thuram provides another dangerous option, while the return of Aurelien Tchouameni and Ibrahima Konate strengthens the spine of the team.

Defensively, Dayot Upamecano is available again after suspension, though injuries to William Saliba and Pierre Kalulu have reduced Zidane’s options.

France know that victory in Milan would secure first place and remove any pressure ahead of their final group match against Turkey.

Italy’s rebuild under Mancini has generated plenty of optimism, and playing at San Siro should give the Azzurri an additional boost.

However, France appear significantly more complete at this stage – a fully developed team, even if they are playing under a new coach. Their squad depth, attacking quality and growing momentum under Zidane make them arguably the strongest team in the group.

Italy will resist as strongly as possible, particularly with Donnarumma behind them, but France’s superior firepower will likely prove decisive.

#1813. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

"Cherki was the difference" 🪄"He is a genius" 🧠Jamie Redknapp reacts to Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City 🔊 pic.twitter.com/UjSarMngDR

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

Anan Khalaili and Takehiro Tomiyasu make their first starts for the hosts tonight and there could be a debut off the bench for Axel Disasi, who joined on loan from Chelsea.

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

There looks set to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager off the visitors’ bench in the form of Ayyoub Bouaddi. There is no Jack Grealish in their squad as his future is up in the air.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

Tonight:Crystal Palace vs Manchester City

Saturday:Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestBournemouth vs EvertonCoventry vs Hull CityTottenham vs Newcastle

Sunday:Chelsea vs BrightonLeeds vs BrentfordSunderland vs FulhamManchester United vs Ipswich

Tonight's team to face Crystal Palace! ​​💪🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Gvardiol, O'Reilly, Anderson, Guéhi, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Kovačić, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/qNgJPXKDM7

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#1812. Serie A preview: Genoa vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

A tough away trip awaits AC Milan on Sunday afternoon, hoping to restore some order against an in-form Genoa side.

What many hoped would be a positive week quickly turned into a negative one, as Milan failed to build on the derby win against Ferencvaros. In other words, they need to respond with a strong performance against Genoa, which is easier said than done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim didn’t have a press conference earlier today due to the tight schedule, so there are no new takeaways from him. Judging from the post-match interviews on Thursday, however, he’s expecting a lot more from his players at the Marassi.

Game date: Sunday, November 8 Kick-off time: 15:00 (CET) Venue: Stadio Luigi Ferraris Referee: Davide Massa (VAR: Camplone)

It’s been said for quite a few games now, but Amorim certainly isn’t being helped by the injury situation. In total, seven players will be on the sidelines for the game tomorrow, including key players like Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic and Alexis Saelemaekers.

Milan were hoping to recover the Serbian for this one, but severe stomach pain is keeping him on the sidelines after missing the Ferencvaros game too. Considering that Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori were already on the injury list, it’s certainly not ideal.

Mike Maignan will be back between the sticks, at least, after serving a suspension in the Europa League. He will have a defence of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan ahead of him, with the left flank being the main worry there.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will be demoted to the bench as Luka Modric will be back from start, partnering with Yunus Musah in a tandem. Adrien Rabiot, meanwhile, is expected to have a slightly more advanced role.

Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will be the danger men on the attacking flanks, looking to replicate their success against Inter in the derby. The same cannot be said for Goncalo Ramos, who instead needs to get going with his goalscoring after bagging just two league goals so far.

In terms of firepower on the bench, Amorim could turn to Davide Bartesaghi, the aforementioned Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse. Francesco Camarda will also be there, of course, but whether he can be categorised as an impact player is a different question.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Modric; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, F. Terracciano, Vladimirov, Bartesaghi, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Pavlovic, Saelemaekers, Terracciano, Tomori.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was signed permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but he did make it clear that Genoa cannot get too cocky.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

This will be the 157th encounter between the two sides, with Milan looking to build on their 71 wins in the fixture, while Genoa are quite far behind at 37 wins. 48 games have ended all square, which is a tally that has increased lately.

In the last five games, there have been three draws (3-3, 0-0 and 1-1), but the good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games. The five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Rossoblu since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. They both left the club on loan this summer, so they won’t be of any help tomorrow.

In the game before that, Rafael Leao (another player who’s no longer in the team) rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa; only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

Starting with Milan, and at the back, I think we should keep an extra eye on Diawara. He did well in the derby but after switching to centre-back for the Ferencvaros game, his display just wasn’t good enough. He will have the same position tomorrow and we need to see an improvement.

Further up the pitch, Moreira showed in the derby that he can be just the X-factor that Milan need, and this game should be an even better one for him (at least on paper). The cameo against Ferencvaros was positive despite the result, so hopefully he can build on the last week.

As for the home side, I’m curious to see Traore in action again. He definitely had some very good games for Sassuolo against the Rossoneri and with more consistent playing time at Genoa, he could rediscover that spark which made him so special.

Finally, I think it would be silly to ignore the defensive general, Vasquez. He always seems to have good games against Milan and honestly, he’s the type of player the Rossoneri could use right now, at least as a deputy.

It’s been incredibly hard to predict how well Milan will do so far this season, with many ups and downs. However, my gut feeling tells me that they will be able to do a whole lot better than on Thursday, especially since the key players are back from start.

My only worry is the left-hand side of the defence, with Diawara and Estupinan set to start there. As such, I’m going to go for a narrow win, with no clean sheet either. Let us know your prediction in the comments below!

#1811. Northampton Town vs Gillingham - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 09 Nov 2026 10:29, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 10:34

Northampton Town welcome Gillingham to Sixfields Stadium on Tuesday night for their third and final EFL Trophy group-stage fixture, with the visitors sitting second in Southern Group G and the Cobblers bottom of the standings.

Northampton have lost both of their opening matches in the competition but could still sneak into the knockout stages with a sizeable victory, provided they can improve their goal difference, while Gillingham know that a point will be enough to secure qualification after Brighton & Hove Albion Under-21s have already played and lost their final group fixture.

Northampton Town's difficult run continued at the weekend as they suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to York City in the opening round of the FA Cup, with the Cobblers falling behind after just 10 seconds.

Only a few months ago, Northampton and their weekend opponents were separated by two divisions, but the Cobblers' relegation from League One and York's promotion mean the two clubs are now competing in League Two after swapping places in the football pyramid.

Under Chris Hogg, Northampton would have been hoping to make an immediate return to the third tier this season, but their early performances suggest that could be a difficult task, with 14 points from 13 league matches leaving them just two points above the relegation zone.

Although the EFL Trophy is unlikely to be a major priority for Hogg and his side, their performances in the competition have been disappointing, particularly after reaching the knockout stages last season.

The Cobblers head into their final group fixture without a point to their name, having suffered defeats to Brighton & Hove Albion Under-21s and Cambridge United in their opening two matches.

As for Gillingham, Gareth Ainsworth's side made a reasonably encouraging start to the 2026-27 League Two campaign, recording five wins, five draws and four defeats from their opening 14 matches to sit just two points outside the automatic promotion places.

The Gills entered Saturday's FA Cup encounter as favourites against National League opposition Barrow, but they were made to work hard at Priestfield Stadium by a side who had gone 10 matches unbeaten in all competitions.

With the tie heading towards extra time, Innes Cameron struck a dramatic stoppage-time winner to secure a 1-0 victory for Gillingham and prevent Barrow from progressing to the second round.

That narrow success has done little to disguise the visitors' inconsistent recent form, however, with Ainsworth's men recording two wins, three defeats and a draw across their last six matches in all competitions.

Nevertheless, Gillingham remain in a strong position to progress from Southern Group G, knowing that a draw on Tuesday would be enough to secure their place in the knockout stages.

Northampton Town form (all competitions):

Northampton will be forced into a change between the posts after goalkeeper Zach Jeacock was forced off with an injury just 12 minutes into their heavy FA Cup defeat against York City.

James Dadge is the most likely candidate to replace him on Tuesday, while Jeacock will join Sam Hoskins in the treatment room, with the latter also unavailable due to a hamstring problem.

Gillingham, meanwhile, have the option of retaining the same starting XI that featured in their most fixture, although Ainsworth is likely to make several changes.

Rohan Luthra started the Gills' previous group match and could replace Oliver Wright in goal, while Bradley Dack is also in contention to return after not featuring since Halloween.

Ainsworth is expected to retain his familiar back three, although Omar Beckles could be rested for the trip to Northampton while former Cobblers striker Tom Eaves could come in to face his former side.

Northampton Town possible starting lineup:

Dadge; Donacien, Moore, Powell, Briggs; Evans; Dale, Fornah, Lemonheigh-Evans, O'Brien-Whitmarsh; Warhurst

Luthra; Dobbs, Smith, Daley; Freeman, McKenzie, Coleman, Brophy; Waldock, Eaves, Dack

With Gillingham in pole position to advance to the next stage of the EFL Trophy, we expect them to make no mistakes here.

We see the away side securing a narrow win that sees them end the group stage with six points from a possible nine before returning to league action next week.
