#1652. England vs. Croatia: Harry Kane's extraordinary international career in numbers ahead of Nations League game

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 10:00, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 17:58

Harry Kane will go down as one of England’s greatest-ever players, a widespread consensus enhanced by his 2026 Ballon d’Or triumph.

At the age of 33, Kane recently became the first Englishman to lift the prestigious individual prize since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane has elevated his game to new heights since swapping his legendary spell at Tottenham Hotspur for Bayern Munich, while he continues to play a significant role on international duty with England.

The prolific striker matched Peter Shilton’s record of 125 international caps for the Three Lions during a UEFA Nations League victory against Czechia last month.

This impressive milestone is the latest record in an extraordinary international career spanning 11-and-a-half years, during which Kane has represented his country at eight major tournaments.

With Kane expected to lead the Three Lions out in Thursday's contest with Croatia at Wembley, Sports Mole provides a statistical breakdown of the striker's international career with England to date.

Kane's journey to drawing level with Shilton at the top of England's all-time appearance charts has been defined by his long-term consistency on the international stage.

Out of his 125 appearances, Kane has been trusted from the first whistle on 111 occasions, amassing nearly 10,000 minutes of international football, and boasting a 66.4% win ratio.

England’s No.9 has represented his country 36 times across major FIFA World Cup and UEFA European Championship tournaments, while he has also made 27 appearances in the UEFA Nations League.

Kane will move above Shilton into outright first position on England’s all-time appearance list when he walks out for his next Three Lions cap (presumable during November’s international break against either Croatia or Spain).

He is also one of only 10 players in history to represent the men’s senior England team at least 100 times.

Men's senior international appearances, all-time

Kane became England’s all-time leading goalscorer in March 2023 when he scored his 54th international goal in a Euro 2024 qualifier against Italy to surpass previous record-holder Wayne Rooney.

Since then, Kane has netted a 37 more goals in 44 appearances for the Three Lions across all competitions, increasing his impressive tally to 91 and closing in on a century of international strikes.

Kane has scored 21 of his goals in major World Cup and Euros tournaments, which includes his six-goal haul at the 2018 World Cup to win the Golden Boot.

Kane has consistently stepped up for England on the biggest stage, ranking third on the all-time list for combined World Cup and European Championship goals (among European players).

The striker has recorded a combined 21 goals in 36 appearances, sitting two behind France star Kylian Mbappe and four adrift of Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo at the top of the pile.

While Kane is England’s record goalscorer at World Cups with 14 goals, he is currently tied with fellow Three Lions great Alan Shearer with seven goals at the European Championship.

European players • World Cup & European Championship finals

Kane marked his England debut with a memorable goal scored just 79 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a comfortable 4-0 home victory over Lithuania in Euro 2016 qualifying.

He took just four months to reach 10 goals for England, while he reached half a century of international goals in June 2022 with a late penalty against Germany to rescue a Nations League draw in Munich.

Kane was also on target from the penalty spot to become England’s all-time record goalscorer in March 2023, before scoring his 75th Three Lions goal in a thumping World Cup qualifying win over Latvia just over two years later.

His most recent England goals came in October 2026 when he scored twice in a 3-0 home victory against Czech Republic in the Nations League.

Goal 1: England 4-0 Lithuania | Wembley Stadium | EURO 2016 Qualifying | March 27, 2015

Goal 10: Scotland 2-2 England | Hampden Park | 2018 FIFA World Cup Qualifying | June 10, 2017

Goal 25: England 4-0 Bulgaria | Wembley Stadium | EURO 2020 Qualifying | September 7, 2019

Goal 50: Germany 1-1 England | Allianz Arena | UEFA Nations League | June 7, 2022

Goal 54: Italy 1-2 England | Stadio Diego Armando Maradona | EURO 2024 Qualifying | March 23, 2023

Goal 75: Latvia 0-5 England | Daugava Stadium | 2026 FIFA World Cup Qualifying | October 14, 2025

Goals 90 & 91: England 3-0 Czechia | Wembley Stadium | UEFA Nations League | October 6, 2026

Across his 11-year international career, Kane has scored against 41 different nations, with Albania proving to be his favourite opponent having netted seven times against them in just four games.

Kane has also scored five goals against Croatia, Czechia and San Marino and four times against Germany, Bulgaria, Malta, Montenegro and Panama.

Meanwhile, Kane has registered four assists in just two matches against Bulgaria - more than a fifth of his total assists for England.

While Kane is widely celebrated for his lethal finishing, he has evolved into one of the world’s elite playmakers for club and country, often seen dropping into deeper positions to link up with his teammates.

Since data logs began tracking assists in late 1979, Kane sits joint-second on the all-time playmaking charts for England, level with Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard and only behind Three Lions icon David Beckham at the top.

Marcandalli hauled him down, yet the referee Davide Massa only saw fit to award a yellow card, and the VAR chief did not deem it necessary to call him over to the monitor for another look. Milan won anyway in the end, but it would have been a totally different game had that been given.

Former referee Gianpaolo Calvarese commented on the incident on his Instagram page and he described Marcandalli’s yellow card as a ‘fair’ decision, which prompted Rabiot to respond in the comments.

“In life, as in football, you can make mistakes. You have to at least be able to admit them. Constantly lying won’t achieve progress, and Italian football is the one that suffers the consequences. Think about it. Bonne soirée,” the Frenchman said.

A post shared by Gianpaolo Calvarese (@gianpaolocalvarese_official)

The relationship between Rabiot and Italian referees has always been characterised by a direct, unfiltered approach. The former PSG man has never been one to hide when he feels he’s suffered an injustice.

He demonstrated this during his time at Juventus. In April 2022, after the defeat against Inter he wrote on Instagram: “It’s difficult to play with 11 against 12.” A year later, in Juventus-Sevilla, he protested again over a denied penalty, even showing the media the marks left by the studs on his leg.

Rabiot brought this to Milan too. After the match against Atalanta on October 18th, for example, he questioned the awarding of bookings, complaining about several uncalled fouls, leading to his famous celebration in front of Chiffi when he scored the 2-0 goal.

#1650. Report - It's over: Liverpool finally ready to call Richard Hughes signing a failure

Liverpool are reportedly looking to replace one Richard Hughes signing. They've made an approach and are ready to rule the deal a failure.

Richard Hughes did a lot of big-money business in charge of Liverpool. He essentially oversaw a complete squad restructuring as the Reds looked to overhaul Jürgen Klopp's group and move onto something new.

Now did that work? No. Was it a good idea? No. Did the job even get completed? No, again.

Liverpool have unquestionably gone backwards since Klopp left. Their squad makes use of virtually none of the youngsters who were being brought through in 2024, while the squad also looks very imbalanced.

The reason? Most of the signings just haven't worked out. There are many, many reasons for that but sometimes they're just the wrong player. And Liverpool are willing to accept failure on at least one of them.

TeamTalk reports that Liverpool are now pushing to sign a new right-back. They claim that an approach was made for Pedro Porro, with the Reds in a group of clubs hoping to sign the Spaniard.

Whether that deal happens or not, it's a sign of the thinking at Anfield. They wanted a new right-back, just 18 months after Hughes signed Jeremie Frimpong for the role from Bayer Leverkusen.

It was a deal that always raised eyebrows. Frimpong was a right wing back in Germany and never really showed an ability to defend in a back four. He was also the sole wide player for Leverkusen and that was never going to be the case at Liverpool.

So the Reds were really asking him to be completely different. Shockingly, that didn't work and Frimpong has struggled to establish himself at the club, ultimately becoming a failed signing - despite a ridiculously unfair situation for him.

It's not his fault that Liverpool signed a player and then asked his game to be completely different. But it does mean that the team needs to move on with a player more suited for the actual role.

Liverpool are apparently trying to do that and it's a sensible move. Even if it does mean giving up on Frimpong.

#1649. Czech Republic vs Spain - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 10 Nov 2026 10:02, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 10:04

Already-qualified Spain will continue their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign with a contest against already-eliminated Czech Republic on Thursday night.

La Roja are currently top of Group A3, three points ahead of second-placed England, while Czech Republic are fourth, losing all four of their matches in the section.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a very difficult Nations League campaign for Czech Republic, who have lost each of their four matches in Group A3.

The Representatives started their 2026-27 campaign with a 2-1 home loss to Croatia, before going down 2-0 at home to England; a 3-1 defeat away to Spain followed, and the national team were then beaten 3-0 by England at Wembley last time out.

Santi Denia's side cannot qualify for the quarter-finals, and they are facing relegation to League B, although it is still possible for them to finish third in this section.

Czech Republic will travel to Croatia in their final game in the section on November 15, and it would be hugely disappointing for the national team if they finished the group without a point.

The Representatives have actually lost six of their last seven matches in all competitions, with their last victory coming in a friendly against Guatemala back in June.

Spain, meanwhile, are safely through to the quarter-finals of the tournament, although they are not yet certain of top position at this stage of proceedings.

La Roja have won all four of their matches in Group A3, scoring 12 goals in the process, and they ended the last international period with a 2-1 success over Croatia.

Luis de la Fuente's side, who won the World Cup in July, beat England 3-2 in their section opener before posting a 4-1 victory over Croatia and a 3-1 win over Czech Republic; Spain are the outstanding team in world football and are regarded as the favourites for the Nations League trophy.

La Roja have won each of their last 11 matches in all competitions, while they have not lost a single match in normal time since March 2024, although the national team were beaten on penalties by Portugal in the final of the 2025 Nations League.

Spain have never lost to Czech Republic, winning six of their previous eight meetings and drawing the other two, so history would be created if the hosts triumph on Thursday.

Czech Republic will be missing Michal Sadilek through suspension, but Ladislav Krejci is available again after serving a ban in the team's last fixture against England.

There should be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Tomas Soucek, who is in line to win his 94th cap for his country, while Vladimir Coufal is expected to feature for the 68th time for Czech Republic at the back.

Adam Hlozek has scored five times in 50 caps and is set to lead the line, while 18-year-old Idris Hopi will hope to make his senior international debut at some stage of the contest.

As for Spain, Lamine Yamal will not be involved, with the 19-year-old nursing a knee injury that he suffered while representing Barcelona against Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

Yamal is expected to link up with the Spain squad after this match, though, to prepare for the game against England on Sunday.

Mikel Oyarzabal will also be a notable absentee for De la Fuente's side due to illness.

Alex Baena and Fermin Lopez are one booking away from being suspended for the clash with England, but both are expected to be in the starting team against Czech Republic.

Kinsky; Coufal, Chaloupek, Krejci, Slama; Kral, Soucek; Cerv, Ambros, Danek; Hlozek

Simon; Porro, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Pedri, Ruiz; N Williams, Fermin, Baena; Torres

Even without Yamal, Spain should be too strong for their opponents on Thursday - it has been a tough campaign for Czech Republic, and we are struggling to back them to secure a positive result here.

#1648. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1645. Opinion: Wonderkid will join Andoni Iraola's squad

Andoni Iraola's time at Liverpool has been recieved differently by members of the Reds' fanbase.

Some feel like he's done a good job with what he has at his disposal and others believe that he should be doing a lot better than he is.

Right now, Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League table and have lost three games across all competitions.

And, while this is slightly better than where they ended the 2025-26 season, it's clear that there are still plenty of improvements that need to be made.

That's why so many transfer links with Liverpool have now started to emerge.

Lucca Brughmans will be joining up with Liverpool's first-team squad next season

Over the summer, four new players were added to Liverpool's first-team squad but, five were signed.

The only player who didn't join up with the Reds this season was KRC Genk's Lucca Brughmans.

The Belgian was signed by Liverpool for £30 million with fans questioning why that much was spent on a relatively unproven 18-year-old goalkeeper.

However, after being sent back on loan to Genk to get some more experience under his belt, Brughmans has brought his game on massively.

Since his return, he's make the goalkeeper spot his own with Liverpool's fans now wondering what their plans for the youngster are next season.

And now, thanks to an update from WinWin Sports, that has been made more than clear.

"Ze Maria, the agent of Brazilian goalkeeper Alisson Becker, who plays for Liverpool FC, revealed the latest developments in negotiations to renew his client's contract with the Reds, in an exclusive interview with winwin," they wrote.

"Ze Maria confirmed to our website that talks with the English club are still in their early stages, saying: 'Alisson loves Liverpool very much. We are in preliminary talks to renew the contract.'

"The agent's statements confirm what the Brazilian goalkeeper himself said, as he expressed his desire to stay at Liverpool beyond his contract, which ends at the end of the current season, confirming his happiness at the English club."

Lucca Brughmans will end up being Alisson's back-up next season

With Alisson's agent saying that they're in talks with Liverpool about extending the Brazilian's contract, it's clear that both parties want him to stay.

And, thanks to the recent performances that he's put in, it's clear why they want that to happen.

On the face of things, this is great news for Liverpool as it means that they won't have to worry about their goalkeeper for another year or two.

The Georgian was initially signed to take over from Alisson in the future but, after his 20 appearances last term, he proved that he wasn't good enough to do that.

This led to Brughmans being signed and, with how well he's been performing for Genk, there's no way that Liverpool will let him go out on loan again.

However, since Alisson is now likely to stay put, the young Belgian will have to become Iraola's number two.

So, not only does this mean that Mamardashvili will have to be moved on but, it also means that the Reds massively believe in Brughmans to meet his potential.

Here's hoping everything works out as Liverpool want it to.

#1644. Charlie wins battle of the Savages! Son scores in 5-0 FA Cup hammering of dad Robbie's Peterborough United - as manager appears to try and supress smile

Published: 17:03 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:26 EST, 7 November 2026

Charlie Savage came out on top in the FA Cup's Battle of the Savages with a goal against his dad Robbie's new team, Peterborough United.

Already two goals up thanks to strikes by Daniel Kyerewaa and Jack Marriott, Reading made a place in round two virtually secure when Robbie's son Charlie added a third in first-half stoppage time.

The midfielder, 23, latched on to a loose ball on the edge of the Peterborough area and fired home, with the aid of a slight deflection, before racing off towards the visiting fans and celebrating with a knee slide.

Dad Robbie, who took over as Posh boss last month after his stint at Forest Green Rovers, looked initially frustrated at his team's defending but you almost sensed a smile given the identity of the goalscorer.

'Charlie Savage's goal is all about him seeing the danger, holding his run, letting it run across his body and finishing,' said former Reading midfielder Steve Sidwell on BBC Sport. 'Reading are deservedly in charge of the game, and Savage has been superb.'

Former Leicester midfielder and Wales international Robbie had feared as much in an exclusive interview with the Daily Mail before the first-round tie.

Charlie Savage scores against his dad Robbie’s side! 😳Reading make it 3-0 at Peterborough! 🔥📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/RmMzxfNIzE

'Charlie Savege's goal is all about him seeing the danger, holding his run, letting it run across his body and finishing,' said former Reading midfielder Steve Sidwell

Savage Jnr celebrates with a knee slide that his dad would have been proud of

Charlie takes advice from the Reading bench as his father Robbie (centre) looks on

'It's going to be horrible,' he had said. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

That particular wish took on a new meaning as his lad lined up to shoot with his left foot to strengthen Reading's vice-like grip on the tie.

Like his dad, Charlie came through Manchester United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

Much the same applied on Saturday night, though this time there were mixed emotions in the Savage household.

It got worse, much worse, as Jamie Reid netted twice in the second half to make it 5-0 to the visitors.

Peterborough can now focus on improving their position from third bottom of League One, while Reading may wish to put thoughts of Wembley to one side as they set their sights on a promotion push.

#1643. Liverpool: Hungary confirm "last-minute" Dominik Szoboszlai decision in new injury update

By Ben Knapton | 10 Nov 2026 10:12

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will remain with the Hungary national team following medical examinations, the Magyars have announced.

The 26-year-old arrived for the November international break carrying a knee injury, which he sustained in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola admitted at full time that Szoboszlai was not feeling 100%, although the former RB Leipzig man nevertheless joined up with his compatriots for the UEFA Nations League.

Hungary issued a statement on Monday morning announcing that Szoboszlai would undergo further medical tests on his knee sprain, which have now been completed, and he will not be sent back to Kirkby.

However, in a fresh update on Tuesday, Hungary also conceded that they are unlikely to make any decisions on Szoboszlai's involvement until the very last minute.

"Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations. Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible," the statement read.

"However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute."

Hungary face Georgia in their penultimate Nations League group-stage game on Saturday, before also taking on Northern Ireland next Tuesday in League B Group 2.

The Magyars currently sit second in the group with seven points from four games, one point adrift of leaders Northern Ireland in top spot, which guarantees promotion to League A.

Hungary's second-placed ranking would see Szoboszlai's side advance to the promotion playoffs, where they would meet a third or fourth-placed team from League A for the right to progress to the top tier.

Szoboszlai came back from the September/October international break with a hamstring injury, which he then exacerbated against Brentford, causing him to miss five games in total for Liverpool so far this season.

As Hungary are vying for League A promotion, and Szoboszlai is arguably their most important player, the Magyars' decision to keep the midfielder around for now is both understandable and defensible.

Liverpool fans will no doubt want the midfielder to withdraw, return to Merseyside and enjoy a complete rest over the international break, and that scenario could still occur if his knee issue flares up over the coming days.

However, Szoboszlai should also do everything in his power to make himself available for his country, thereby forcing Liverpool fans to watch on anxiously over the next week.

#1640. Opinion: Sign him, Liverpool: South American star is screaming 'come and get me'

One South American Premier League star is just begging for Liverpool to sign him. It's time to get a deal done.

Liverpool have a selection of superstars in their squad right now. That's the result of an unprecedented spend over the last couple of years, with the Reds repeatedly breaking their transfer record.

It was viewed as the way to go post-Jurgen Klopp. They wanted to sign as much talent as possible, taking advantage of the position that Klopp left them in, essentially.

The result? It's not a great squad. The talent pool is fantastic, no question there, but Liverpool have been unable to piece things together to create a bigger picture.

He's played all but 23 minutes in the Premier League for the side currently in second and is the kind of player that elite teams thrive with - someone who wins the ball back, makes lots of runs, and pops up with incredible moments.

We've seen two of those this season. The first was a ridiculous goal from halfway. The second was a sensational goal against Brentford this weekend that was essentially a "come and get me plea" to any top clubs looking for that 'glue' player.

We wrote back in August that Gomez is the kind of player Liverpool need. Our Value Adder model is one that pushes him as as an incredibly valuable footballer who's still only 23 and flying under the radar.

Now, he's no longer flying particularly far under that radar. People are picking him up thanks to these wonder goals. But with Brighton almost certainly facing massive offers for their bigger 'stars' in 2027, we think there's a chance to tempt them with an offer here.

Gomez is what Liverpool need. He's worth a fortune to a club like the Reds who are just a player or two away from having a very balanced team.

#1639. ST MIRREN 0 RANGERS 2: It's back to the grind for McInnes' men as they show grit to see off Buddies

By KEVIN MCKENNA AT MARBILL COACHES STADIUM

Published: 17:42 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:51 EST, 7 November 2026

At some stage, you would suspect Rangers are going to find their groove under Derek McInnes.

But until then, they will happily settle for just getting points on the board. How they go about it doesn’t really matter in the grand scheme of things.

This hard-fought victory in Paisley — much like so many of Rangers’ Premiership wins this season — was all about substance over style.

Yes, there were flashes of quality here and there. But it was more to do with doing the ugly stuff well than anything else. Fortunately for McInnes, his side are proving to be adept at doing so.

It’s a handy habit to have at their disposal. We saw it in recent draws at Dundee and Hearts last month, managing to come away with something when they probably deserved nothing.

With nobody knowing what version of Celtic are going to turn up on any given week, all Rangers can do is stay within touching distance of the league leaders — a point in front ahead of their meeting with Kilmarnock this afternoon — until they come to blows again in the new year.

Rangers skipper Neil nets with the aid of a deflection to put his side two goals up

Rangers wasted no time getting themselves on the front foot. St Mirren barely got a kick in the opening exchanges, and on the odd occasion they did, possession was turned over far too easily.

Badredine Bouanani had the visitors’ first effort of the night on six minutes, cutting inside from the right flank before pulling the trigger from 20 yards, but it lacked the power to properly test Jacob Chapman in the Saints goal.

The keeper had to be far more alert five minutes later, pulling off a wonderful reaction stop to deny Ryan Naderi finishing off Kevin Kelsy’s headed knockdown. You would have put your house on the in-form Czech finding the net.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed over from the resulting corner.

Having finally settled down, St Mirren gave their opponents a perfect opportunity to take the lead, when Samuel Ramos brought down James Penrice on the angle of the Buddies’ box.

There didn’t appear to be a great deal of contact, but it didn’t take long for VAR to confirm referee Nick Walsh’s decision.

Naderi stepped up to do what he failed to do moments earlier, coolly slotting into the bottom corner to register his ninth goal in all competitions this season.

From looking as if he was likely to be on his way out of Ibrox over the summer, the 23-year-old has become one of the first names on McInnes’ team sheet.

Penrice goes down under Ramos' challenge to earn Rangers a penalty in the first half

And perhaps the most exciting thing from a Rangers perspective is that he is still a million miles from being the finished article. But playing with this sort of confidence, he’s only going to get better.

He was involved in a lovely free-flowing counter shortly after the half-hour mark, with the ball eventually falling to Kim Min-su on the penalty spot. However, the South Korean delayed getting his shot off and the chance was gone.

When running full-flight at defences, the 20-year-old is a delight to watch in that No10 role.

There isn’t anyone in the country better at finding pockets of space between the lines and taking the ball on the turn. But for all that there is to enjoy about his game, his decision-making in the key moments undoubtedly needs work.

A woeful ball out from Olwethu Makhanya set up a two-v-two for the hosts before the break, with Ramos drilling straight at Ivor Pandur from inside the area. With the whole goal to aim at, the Spaniard should have done much better.

The same goes for Jake Young, who blasted high and wide from a promising position a minute later.

Naderi is hailed by Min-su after putting the visitors ahead from the spot

As dominant as Rangers were, you never got the feeling their lead was particularly secure, such is their tendency to play themselves into trouble every now and then.

Fernandez is the worst culprit for it. Fortunately for him, his recovery pace gets him out of jail more often than not. He needed it on a couple of occasions here.

A delightful threaded ball from Bouanani found the feet of Min-su inside the box on 47 minutes but under heavy pressure, he was unable to prod beyond Chapman who’d rushed off his line to meet him. It was hard to be too critical of the Rangers midfielder this time.

Chapman was once again called into action to thwart Kelsy from close range after the Venezuelan escaped the clutches of his marker to collect Min-su’s pass in behind.

He then skewed an effort wide at the back post from an excellent Nico Raskin delivery from the right. It was a night on which very little came off for the big man in front of goal.

To his credit, he kept plugging away, and played a key role in Rangers’ doubling their advantage just after the hour mark, with his driving run causing a bit of chaos in the Buddies backline, before captain Dan Neil swept a loose ball into the bottom corner via the aid of a big deflection to give Chapman absolutely no chance of saving.

With his first touch, substitute Eseosa Sule wasted a glorious chance to reduce the deficit after being left all alone at the back post to stab home Declan John’s cross.

With the ball seemingly destined for the back of the net, Rangers keeper Pandur produced a stunning save on the stretch to turn the ball round the post.

The Croatian’s signing went somewhat under the radar over the summer, but he has demonstrated time and time again that he is a man for the big occasion. He’ll win this side plenty of points between now and the end of the season.

McInnes applauds the away support after signing off for the international break with a win

St Mirren came into this one having won just once in their past eight, but you wouldn’t have guessed they were struggling for confidence given the way in which they threw everything at the game in an effort to get a result.

It wasn’t for lack of trying, with Luke Thomas testing Pandur from range before Calvin Ramsay’s follow-up header clipped the post.

That would be as close as Saints would come, as Rangers dug in to grind out an ugly — but ultimately deserved — win on the road.

They will need to be far better, far more consistently if they want to get their hands on the Premiership title come May. But that’s a worry for another day.

#1638. San Marino vs Belarus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 10 Nov 2026 10:14, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 20:39

Belarus make the trip to San Marino on Thursday evening looking for the win that could see them end the night sitting in top spot of Group C1 in the UEFA Nations League.

Meanwhile, San Marino head into the game in Serravalle assured of bottom spot having lost all four of their matches.

Having suffered defeat in Albania in their opening contest, Belarus essentially gifted control of the group to that nation and Finland.

However, a return of seven points from their following three games has left Belarus sitting in second position, two points behind Albania who have been far from convincing in this group.

Four of the seven points that Belarus have acquired have been against Finland, Viktor Goncharenko's side earning a 1-0 victory last time out.

They are also on a run of three consecutive clean sheets, not conceding a goal for seven halves of football in this competition.

Furthermore, Belarus have only suffered one defeat in 10 games across all tournaments. As well as wins in the likes of Cyprus and Armenia, they have earned a draw in Denmark, albeit back on November 15, 2025.

As far as San Marino are concerned, they will be bitterly disappointed to have conceded 16 goals across four matches at this level.

Despite being viewed as the clear minnows of the group after promotion from League D, shipping 10 goals in their opening home double-header versus Finland and Albania effectively left them out of contention.

To their credit, it took a 93rd-minute goal from Albania to inflict a 2-1 defeat on the 211th-ranked side in the world rankings when they met on October 6.

While Roberto Cevoli will take positives from that near-miss, San Marino remain without a win since November 2024, when they recorded a 3-1 victory in Liechtenstein in the last edition of the Nations League.

San Marino will make at least two changes for this fixture, a consequence of centre-back Michele Cevoli being left out of the squad due to injury and striker Nicolas Giacopetti serving a one-match ban.

Marco Pasolini is expected to deputise in the middle of the defence, while the experienced Nicola Nanni could return in attack.

Lorenzo Lazarri is an alternative in midfield having scored as a substitute in Albania.

With Belarus duo Artem Shumanskiy and German Barkovskiy serving one-match bans, Artem Kontsevoy and Vitaliy Lisakovich may be drafted into the final third.

The away side could also make a change on the right flank with Anton Kovalev potentially being handed a start.

Colombo; Fabbri, Pasolini, Rossi, Giocondi; Meloni, Della Balda, Capicchioni, Zannoni; Salicioni, Nanni

Lapoukhov; Kalinin, Volkov, Gomanov, Pechenin; Bocherov, Selyava; Kovalev, Ebong, Kontsevoy; Lisakovich

As with the other games involving San Marino, we expect this to be largely one-way traffic. However, the minnows may be able to restrict Belarus to a goal in each half to add some respectability to the result.

#1637. Cisse discusses humble beginnings, choosing Milan, Italy call-up, Amorim and amazing form

Alphadjo Cisse has shed some light on his journey to becoming an AC Milan player, as well as what his first few months at the club have been like.

It has been a simply remarkable rise for Cisse, who at the start of 2026 was playing in the second division with Catanzaro, on loan from Hellas Verona. Milan bought him from there but left him with his loan club, before a serious injury needed surgery and ruled him out for the rest of the season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Fast-forwarding to early November, and the 20-year-old is currently the top scorer for the Rossoneri with eight goals, the most recent of which came in Sunday’s 2-1 win over Genoa. There is talk of an imminent renewal already, while Roberto Mancini gave him a senior Italy call-up.

Cisse gave an exclusive interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio in which he touched upon various topics from his upbringing to the brilliant moment he is currently experiencing. MilanNews relayed his words.

“My life changed in my father’s factory. A Verona manager went to meet him at work to beg him to take me to their place. He’d been a worker forever: every day he’d leave work at 5:00pm, and by 5:15 he was already outside our house, calling me and taking me to play soccer.

“I still remember the first time. It was afternoon. He came up to the house and said, ‘Come on, I’ll take you somewhere’. And we went to the pitch. He was the one who instilled in me the passion for soccer, and from that moment on, I’ve never stopped.

“My parents made so many sacrifices to support me on this journey: my mom, when she had days off from work, would come up with me to take me on the bus to practice.”

“My mom is a very demanding mom. But she helps me stay focused and prevent fame from overwhelming me. So everything becomes easier with her. They tell me every day that they’re proud of me, but they also do everything they can to keep me grounded.

“Carlos, Milan’s assistant coach, often tells me this too: ‘ Surround yourself with people who truly love you and who help you stay focused’. I’m sure of this: I carry with me the carefree attitude of the child I was. I play with a smile. It’s hard not to have that in these first few months.”

You have just been called up by the Italian national team for the first time…

“I was on my way to do the pre-match interview against Ferencváros in the Europa League and they stopped me to say, ‘Alpha, they’ve called you up to the national team… the senior team!’ I had the match, I only realised afterwards.

“I want to prove I can compete. The call was in the air, they’d been talking to me about it for days… but this is my big chance. I haven’t had the chance to stop and think about my career. Football moves fast.”

“A few weeks ago, they asked me how much of my potential as a player I’d shown. I said 70%. Can I say that? Maybe I need to lower it a bit… let’s say 40%, because I have so many aspects to improve on, but at the same time, I know who I am and what I’m worth.

“Last season, Aquilani – who was my coach at Catanzaro – told me that ‘if you don’t play at least 10 years in Serie A, I think you’ll have failed’. I took it as a positive motivation, a phrase that pushed me to always do better and believe in what I can do.

“One of my friends in football is Favasuli, I met him just last year in Serie B. We often found ourselves talking… daydreaming. I still remember the day he said to me: ‘Think about when one day we’ll face two great teams’.

“I smiled. ‘It would be great to meet again in Serie A, but maybe it’s a little too late for me, I’m already 23…’ Instead, he made it too: Milan-Napoli will be in December, we’ll see. He was my driver, he drove me to camp. He’s proof that there’s no age to stop feeling young or believing in it, no matter the path.”

Your path has already taken you from Verona to Catanzaro and to Milan…

“In those very months, my life changed again. No longer in my father’s factory. In a matter of days, I had gone from wondering how far I was from Serie A to finding myself facing the most important decision of my career.

“I’ll be honest: I didn’t take that moment very well. When I arrived at Catanzaro, I had only played two five-minute games in Serie A, including against AC Milan. Aquilani and manager Polito really wanted me, they pushed me. It was my first experience away from home.

“In just a few months, I scored a lot, everyone wanted me. And in January, I was practically on a flight to Holland, bound for Rotterdam: to sign with PSV. But then AC Milan came along.”

“My friends’ WhatsApp group exploded: ‘Alpha, is it true?!’ And I was like, ‘Yes guys, yes!’ I didn’t want to make the wrong choice: PSV wanted me right away, while Milan would have let me finish the season in Serie B.

“Two great teams, but Milan… how do you explain that? I was experiencing a mix of emotions; my parents told me to stay calm and that the best was yet to come. We decided this was the right choice. And judging by how things are going, I’d say we were right.”

“The first few times I came to Milanello, I did so to recover from my injury. Milan left me at Catanzaro, yes, but after a few days I got injured. In fact, I had serious doubts: ‘I’m coming to AC Milan after an injury, let’s see how it goes’.

“This is exactly what Amorim spoke to me about as soon as we met. We focused on the injury, and he explained what he expected of me on the pitch. He’s a great guy, and he knows how to deal with us young players. And he knows how to keep me grounded. Even though I’m not someone who likes to let my mind wander.”

You kept a promise after your Europa League hat-trick…

“Even after my hat-trick in the Europa League, I have to say that everything was already clear to me: it was simply confirmation to myself that I can compete at this level. I didn’t see it as a point of arrival, but as a promise kept to the child I was.

“And above all, as a promise to keep. Even though I was coming back from a long injury, even though I’m young and have so many areas to improve, I never had any doubts about my abilities or where I could go. I’m very demanding of myself, just like my mother.”

“Modrić gave me some advice on what I need to improve: I need to read the game better and understand the moments of the match. He’s a great player, a spectacular person, willing to help you learn, and interesting to listen to.

“Even though my idol was very different as a kid: Paul Pogba, when he was at Juventus. We do different things on the pitch, and his haircut certainly didn’t go unnoticed by a kid… maybe I’ll get one in the future! What I appreciated about him was that he made people laugh: that’s what I want to do too.

“I was inspired by the player whose jersey I had as a child: Clarence Seedorf. My mother gave it to me; it was the one I wore on the pitch. So maybe it was just my destiny to come here. Seedorf became an idol at San Siro.

“The place where you feel the grandeur, the pressure, the feeling of playing in a stadium that represents a childhood dream. Being there now is like saying to the child I was: ‘See? You did it’. It’s a huge motivation for me. But I’m carefree enough not to be affected by it.

“When you start playing, you notice it less and you don’t pay attention: it’s easier. The fans are incredibly attached to the team. You notice it not just in Milan, but all over the world. And that’s how you understand where you are. I was really impressed by the organisation here.”

Do you like to play with a certain freedom?

“I’m very carefree when I go on the pitch. Whether it’s playing in Serie B or going to San Siro, I think it’s normal for me. I’m the same person I always am. As a kid, I was obsessed with bicycle kicks. I scored five or six incredible goals… now I avoid them!

“In the Verona youth team, I had a coach, Paolo Sammarco, who shaped the way I play today: he gave me a lot of freedom, helping me understand how I should express myself.”

Is it important for young Italian players to have confidence?

“Italy is full of strong young players, I assure you. It all depends on the opportunities you’re given. Many have emerged in recent months, including me, and I’m sure many more will emerge in the near future.

“When you reach a certain level, you’re amazed: one above all, I was struck by Pisilli, he’s simply amazing. I knew him, but when I played with him, I understood his strength. And I understood my own strength when, in my early years in Verona, I approached the big boys.

“The level was rising, but I continued to have faith, to understand that I could achieve great things if I followed the path I had. That I had something special.”

Your life has changed a lot, are you still the same person?

“My life has changed so much in the past few months, perhaps more than I can even realize. There are moments when I stop and think about how different everything is from just a short while ago. Football is taking me to places I dreamed of, but inside I’m still the same boy.

“But I know what my ambitions are. And perhaps that’s exactly what helps me not lose myself, even when everything changes. I try to enjoy every moment, without forgetting where I started from and all the people who have accompanied me to this point.”

Finally, clear something up: how do you say your name?

“My name is Cisse, without an accent. My name can be read any way, but it’s pronounced ‘Sisse’. I even had to send a voice message to the commentators!”

#1635. Germany squad: Five players to watch under Jurgen Klopp this month including 17-year-old wunderkind

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 10:20

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has drastically trimmed his squad ahead of two crucial UEFA Nations League fixtures against Serbia and the Netherlands during the November international break.

Facing a must-win double-header, Die Mannschaft are in danger of failing to qualify for the quarter-finals as they currently sit third in League A Group C, three points behind both of their upcoming opponents.

Germany will first travel to Belgrade to face Serbia on Friday, before returning home to host the Netherlands in a blockbuster clash at the Olympiastadion in Berlin next Monday.

From history-making teenage playmakers to reborn Bundesliga stars and Premier League luminaries, Klopp's 24-man squad is a fascinating blend of elite experience and explosive youth.

These two crunch matches present the ultimate stage for several international hopefuls to cement their place under Klopp, and here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at five Germany players to watch out for during this month's international break.

The surprise inclusion to Klopp’s latest squad is Borussia Monchengladbach’s wunderkind Wael Mohya, who has earned his first-ever senior call-up for Germany ahead of his 18th birthday next month.

The 2008 Mettmann-born starlet, who is of Moroccan descent through his parents, broke into Monchengladbach’s senior team midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since been linked with the likes of Bayern and Liverpool in recent months, having developed into an increasingly influential figure under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all nine Bundesliga games as well as two DFB-Pokal matches.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in back-to-back matches last month, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 victory over Stuttgart – Monchengladbach’s only league win of the season to date.

The dynamic teenage attacker, comfortable operating centrally and as a winger on either flank, is blessed with superb close control and an innate ability to operate comfortably with both feet, offering Klopp a highly creative, versatile midfield weapon.

Mohya, who has received eight Germany youth caps between Under-16 and Under-21 level, is undeniably one to watch this month as he bids to become the third-youngest senior international in German history and bring his fearless club form onto the Nations League stage.

An explosive start to the 2026-27 campaign by striker Niclas Fullkrug has been rewarded with a return to the Germany national team squad for the first time since September 2025.

The veteran marksman endured difficult spells at both West Ham United and AC Milan, but he is enjoying a remarkable revival on loan at Werder Bremen, where he began his career 15 years ago.

At the age of 33, Fullkrug has proven that age is just a number by plundering a ruthless nine goals in as many Bundesliga appearances so far this season, firing him to the top of the division’s scoring charts and already five clear of Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Fullkrug’s lethal aerial presence and old-school, back-to-goal physical profile offer Germany a genuine focal point with qualities that differ to both Kai Havertz and Younes Ebnoutalib who will also battle for the No.9 role under Klopp.

If Germany are to breach the backlines of Serbia and the Netherlands this month, Fullkrug's predatory instincts inside the penalty area could be paramount should he be selected to lead the line.

Having made his senior international debut under Klopp during the previous window, Koln’s crown jewel has done more than enough to maintain his place in this refined 24-man squad.

The highly-rated 20-year-old winger has seamlessly transitioned his dominant youth form into the Bundesliga, contributing to 18 goals (13 goals, five assists) in 34 top-flight matches last season to help Koln avoid relegation.

This term, El Mala has found the net five times in 10 appearances in all competitions, including a late consolation strike against Bayer Leverkusen last weekend, and his strong performances continue to be monitored by a number of Europe’s biggest clubs.

Boasting rare physical traits for a wide player at 6ft 2in, El Mala pairs raw explosive pace with clinical goalscoring instincts, and his ability to drive vertically at opposing full-backs provides a unique dynamic to a German attack that has typically favoured shorter, intricate passing combinations.

With Klopp eager to establish a permanent threat on the flanks, El Mala represents a intriguing tactical alternative for this month's double-header while the likes of Karim Adeyemi, Serge Gnabry, Leroy Sane, Chris Fuhrich, Jamie Leweling and Kevin Schade all watch on from afar.

Having initially been left out of Klopp’s squad, Ridle Baku has received a late call-up to the Germany set-up after Waldemar Anton was forced to withdraw over the weekend due to injury.

The right-back has played 12 times for a Leipzig side who sit fourth in the Bundesliga table and has chipped in with three goals, with his qualities on full display in a narrow Champions League defeat to Man City last week in which he fired home a second-half equaliser.

The 28-year-old right-back has not featured for the national team since earning his eighth cap in November last year, but this window offers a massive opportunity for him to revitalise his international career.

Baku will face stern competition for starts at right-back from Freiburg's Philipp Treu who was preferred for the previous international window and made a notable impression during his maiden Germany outing.

However, having two strong right-back options battling it out against each other would enable Klopp to continue with captain Joshua Kimmich as a central midfielder, where his tactical intelligence and elite passing range can orchestrate the play.

In the absence of injured star Jamal Musiala, Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz carries the creative burden for Klopp’s Germany side and will hope to transfer his recent form at club level onto the international stage.

Wirtz has previously come under fire for failing to make the desired impact at Liverpool, but he ranks joint-second for chances created in the Premier League so far this season (22) and has contributed to four goals in his last four top-flight appearances.

After setting up goals in wins over Brighton and Brentford, Wirtz scored and assisted in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, helping Andoni Iraola’s side climb back into the top four.

At 23 years of age, Wirtz is in fact one of the more experienced players in Klopp’s squad, as his 48 international caps is only bettered by three players (Kimmich, Havertz and Jonathan Tah).

Having captained Germany in their last Nations League match, Wirtz will be tasked with orchestrating the offensive tempo from the number 10 role as the battle for knockout qualification reaches a boiling point.

He will aim to replicate his man-of-the-match display in last month's 2-0 win over Serbia in which he scored and assisted.

#1634. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo
